title: client-clock-drift-reconciliation-for-consistent-metering
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We observe duplicate usage and quota mis-attribution when clients retry requests with client-side timestamps that drift relative to server time. Because rate windows and quota accounting are currently keyed partially on the client-provided timestamp and per-request fingerprinting, clock skew + network retries can cause the same logical request to be counted in adjacent windows or trigger multiple quota charges. This is most visible for mobile SDK users and edge proxies behind NAT where clock synchronization is unreliable.

Proposal (high level): Introduce a server-led clock-reconciliation layer and conservative canonicalization rules so that billing and quota windows are computed against a reconciled time for each client identity. Key elements: 1) lightweight per-client skew estimate maintained in the metering service (rolling EWMA of observed client_time - server_time). 2) when a request arrives, compute a reconciled timestamp = client_time - skew_estimate (bounded by a configurable max skew correction, e.g., 12s). 3) use reconciled timestamp for window assignment and de-duplication matching (fingerprint + reconciled timestamp window) instead of raw client_time. 4) support optional client monotonic sequence id to provide strong de-duplication for clients that can produce it; fall back to reconciled timestamp algorithm for legacy clients. 5) provide a short-lived server ingestion token in the response (ingest_token) that clients can store and reuse to safely retry without additional charge.

Why this is different from current idempotency work: existing approaches focus on opaque replay tokens, global nonces, or ledger reconciliation. This design targets the root cause (clock skew leading to window misalignment) and adds a low-cost reconciliation step that prevents otherwise-sane retries from being double-charged across adjacent windows. It is intentionally tolerant: we do not force clock sync or require clients to upgrade immediately.

Non-goals: forcing clock synchronization, replacing existing idempotency primitives, or eliminating server-side dedupe entirely.

Telemetry impact: we will add metrics for skew_estimate distribution, percentage of requests that were corrected by >1s, and duplicate-detection reductions per-customer after rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Server maintains a per-client skew estimate and applies it to assign reconciled timestamps for incoming requests
Reconciled timestamps are used for rate window assignment and de-duplication; duplicates that would previously have fallen in adjacent windows are now grouped and only billed once
Fallback: clients without sequence ids see no functional change other than reduced duplicate billing; clients with sequence ids can opt-in to stronger de-duplication with ingest_token
Benchmarks show <5% p95 increase in metering service tail latency at target qps when skew correction is enabled
New metrics available in Console showing reduction in cross-window duplicates and per-customer duplicate billing incidents
implementation_notes: Add a SkewEstimator component to metering-api: lightweight per-client EWMA maintained in Redis with TTL 24h; keys are customer_id + client_fingerprint
Reconciled timestamp = clamp(client_ts - skew_estimate, server_now - max_out_of_order, server_now + max_future_tolerance)
Default configuration: max_out_of_order = 30s, max_future_tolerance = 5s, skew EWMA alpha = 0.2
If client provides a monotonic sequence_id header, prefer sequence_id + customer_id + model_hash as primary dedupe key; reconciled timestamp used only as secondary guard
Issue changes to API docs and SDKs (Go, Python, JS) introducing optional 'sequence_id' and reporting of ingest_token on successful ingest
Metering-worker de-dupe algorithm updated to use reconciled windows for grouping; reconciliation pass for historical receipts will be a separate job (see migration)
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'clock_reconciliation' flag at customer and global levels
Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal test projects and 3 low-traffic customers; collect skew telemetry and duplicate-rate baselines (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (beta): enable opt-in for customers via Console toggle; SDKs add conditional sequence_id wiring; monitor duplicates and latencies (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (default on): flip global default to enabled for new customers; existing customers get migration guidance and opt-out for 8 weeks before enforced
Emergency rollback: disable feature flag at runtime; re-enable legacy dedupe keys for safety
migration_notes: Run a one-off reconciliation job that scans last 72h of ingests and emits candidate duplicate groups where timestamps differ by <= max_out_of_order and fingerprint matches — mark but do not retroactively refund during initial rollout
After 8 week observation window, consider automated retroactive consolidation for customers with high duplicate incidence (requires billing/legal approval)
SDKs should start sending sequence_id and handle ingest_token; provide backward-compatible serverside behavior if values absent
test_plan: Unit tests for SkewEstimator with synthetic skew traces (including leap seconds and big jumps)
Integration test: simulated client with clock drift + retry policy should result in single billed event when sequence_id provided and when relying solely on reconciled timestamp
Load test: metering service under expected qps with skew correction enabled; measure p50/p95/p99 latency and Redis ops
Chaos test: random clock leaps on client side and transient Redis errors to validate graceful degradation
E2E: enable in staging and run rate-limit and quota acceptance tests across small/medium/large customers
observability_and_metrics: metering.reconciled_count (number of requests assigned reconciled timestamps)
metering.duplicate_reduction_rate (percent fewer duplicate bill events vs baseline)
metering.skew_corrections_over_threshold (count of requests with correction > configured threshold)
alert: customer_duplicate_billing_rate > 0.5% increase vs baseline for >30m
open_questions: What is the appropriate per-customer TTL for skew estimates for ephemeral clients? (default 24h proposed)
Do we need stronger privacy constraints on storing client_fingerprint? Consider hashing and salt per-customer
Should reconciled timestamp become the canonical source for quota enforcement or only used for de-dupe? (proposal: both, but enable via feature flag)
Legal/billing: what level of retroactive consolidation/refunds do we support once duplicates are detected?
Operational: Redis cost and cardinality impact for high-cardinality client_fingerprints
